claim: Self-consistency replaces greedy chain-of-thought decoding by sampling a diverse set of reasoning paths and marginalizing to the most consistent (majority) final answer, requiring n independent generations per prompt rather than one.
stance_target: mechanism definition of self-consistency, the multi-sample method being made cheap in the AAAI-27 project
quoted_support: It first samples a diverse set of reasoning paths instead of only taking the greedy one, and then selects the most consistent answer by marginalizing out the sampled reasoning paths.

claim: Self-consistency decoding boosts accuracy substantially over greedy chain-of-thought decoding: GSM8K +17.9%, SVAMP +11.0%, AQuA +12.2%, StrategyQA +6.4%, ARC-challenge +3.9%.
stance_target: sampling multiple reasoning paths yields large accuracy gains, motivating why multi-sample methods are valuable despite their cost
scope_conditions: arithmetic and commonsense reasoning benchmarks; PaLM and UL2 model families
quoted_support: Our extensive empirical evaluation shows that self-consistency boosts the performance of chain-of-thought prompting with a striking margin on a range of popular arithmetic and commonsense reasoning benchmarks, including GSM8K (+17.9%), SVAMP (+11.0%), AQuA (+12.2%), StrategyQA (+6.4%) and ARC-challenge (+3.9%).

claim: Self-consistency was originally proposed as a decoding-time accuracy-improvement strategy, not as a confidence/uncertainty-quantification method; its later use as a confidence signal (agreement rate across samples as a calibration score) is a downstream repurposing not present in the original 2022 paper.
stance_target: origin and scope of self-consistency as later used for confidence calibration
scope_conditions: based on the paper's stated framing as a decoding strategy for accuracy
quoted_support: In this paper, we propose a new decoding strategy, self-consistency, to replace the naive greedy decoding used in chain-of-thought prompting.
